text:
COP gained 0.89% today to $136.80, steadying after a rough two-week slide of 8.2%. The modest recovery came as oil prices held relatively stable—US crude at $99.64 and Brent at $107.03—with the stock bouncing off its low point of $134.47 from just two trading days ago. The rebound appears to reflect a pause in selling pressure rather than a new catalyst; the stock has been choppy throughout the period without a clear directional trigger.

The two-week decline reflects a real shift in energy market sentiment: Brent crude dipped below $90 per barrel last week on hopes the Iran conflict could ease, and while President Trump has suggested a resolution could come "fairly soon," the uncertainty around geopolitical risk in the Middle East is keeping crude prices volatile and weighing on oil company valuations. For a major oil producer, lower crude prices directly shrink the dollar value of every barrel they extract, which is why the stock fell hard when those peace hopes spiked.
